memory_update.text: FORM should remain a high-priority underfollowed HBM sub-supplier candidate because company sources explicitly connect its probe cards to SK hynix HBM testing and HBM4 collaboration.
CAMT should remain a high-priority HBM inspection/metrology candidate because company news shows repeated HBM and OSAT advanced-packaging orders, including a June 2026 order exceeding $105 million.

KLIC belongs in the advanced-packaging bonding-equipment watchlist, but its HBM exposure should be treated as inference until customer/order evidence shows direct HBM qualification or material HBM-related revenue.

Need next-layer verification for HBM-specific revenue mix, customer concentration, order durability, tool-of-record status, backlog, capacity constraints, and qualification cycles across FORM, CAMT, KLIC, and ONTO.
FORM should be tracked as a direct HBM/advanced-packaging probe-card candidate; verify HBM-specific revenue, backlog, and customer concentration.
CAMT has direct evidence of HBM-manufacturer order exposure and should be tracked as an advanced-packaging inspection/metrology candidate.
Thermo-compression bonding, wafer-level probe, advanced-packaging inspection/metrology, and burn-in before/after HBM integration are the most promising US-listed sub-supplier branches for this node.

Need deeper verification for HBM-specific revenue exposure at KLIC and AEHR; current evidence supports relevance to advanced packaging and AI/HBM package economics, not confirmed direct HBM supplier status.

FORM should remain a priority underfollowed HBM sub-supplier because it has direct Q1 2026 evidence of record DRAM revenue driven by HBM applications and product-level evidence for HBM stack/interposer testing.

CAMT is one of the strongest direct-evidence names in the node after June 2026 orders from a tier-1 OSAT and leading HBM manufacturer, plus Hawk platform positioning for HBM, chiplets, hybrid bonding, and micro-bump inspection.

For HBM and advanced packaging, the best underfollowed US-listed sub-supplier lanes appear to be probe cards, inspection/metrology, and bonding equipment; generic semiconductor equipment screens may miss these narrower exposures.

COHU remains a possible shadow candidate in sockets/contactors/handlers and semiconductor test interfaces, but this pass did not find HBM-specific evidence strong enough to include it over FORM, CAMT, KLIC, and AMKR.
FORM is the clearest US-listed reference anchor for HBM probe-card exposure, but attention may already be medium-to-high after explicit HBM revenue disclosures.
KLIC should be tracked as an underfollowed HBM/advanced-packaging equipment candidate because its legacy wire-bonding label may obscure fluxless thermocompression and first-HBM-system optionality.
CAMT has unusually direct HBM evidence for an inspection/metrology supplier via disclosed orders from a leading HBM manufacturer and tier-1 OSAT.
ONTO is a broader advanced-packaging process-control candidate; keep it in Layer 1B but require proof of HBM-specific revenue rather than generic advanced-packaging exposure.

Need a later pass on US-listed materials and consumables candidates for underfill, bonding materials, substrates, dicing, thermal interface materials, and ABF/glass-core substrate adjacency; evidence in this pass was stronger for tools and inspection than for materials.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the US-listed universe for direct public companies exposed to HBM and advanced-packaging sub-supplier bottlenecks. The best-fit candidates in this pass are not HBM producers but enabling tool, test, inspection, metrology, and bonding-equipment suppliers. FormFactor and Camtek have the clearest HBM-specific evidence from company sources. Kulicke & Soffa has direct advanced-packaging thermocompression bonding exposure but HBM linkage is broader and should be verified at the customer/order level. Onto Innovation is a larger process-control and advanced-packaging tools name with AI/advanced-packaging evidence, but HBM-specific revenue sensitivity needs further confirmation. Expanded the US-listed universe for the HBM / advanced-packaging sub-supplier node with a two-lane funnel. Reference lane is intentionally light; the main candidates are specialized equipment, test, inspection/metrology, and bonding suppliers that sit one layer below memory producers, foundries, OSATs, and AI accelerator customers. Strongest directly evidenced exposure in this pass: FORM probe cards for HBM/advanced packaging and CAMT inspection/metrology with disclosed HBM-manufacturer orders. KLIC and AEHR are included as underfollowed hypotheses tied to thermo-compression bonding and AI/HBM package burn-in economics, respectively; both require customer and HBM-specific revenue verification before surviving later layers.
